Fmr. Amb. John Bolton to Plead GUILTY in Classified Documents Case

In October of 2025, former ambassador and national security advisor John Bolton was hit with an 18-count indictment for retention and transmission of National Defense Information. He pleaded NOT GUILTY and hired infamous D.C. attorney Abbe Lowell.

According to the indictment, Bolton, during his time in the first Trump Administration, had been taking lots of notes on his meetings and briefings, jotting what was discussed, who said what, etc., during high-level meetings. Of course all of what happened in these meetings was highly classified. And naturally, so were his notes.

But Bolton didn't care. His notes were a meal ticket. He was planning on cashing in on his time in the White House. He was going to write a "tell-all book," do the talk show circuit, and become a regular pundit on legacy media networks.

So Bolton wrote drafts of his future tell-all book based on the notes he took and sent those drafts to his wife and daughter. They would read them and give him feedback. He also sent drafts to his publishing agent. These drafts also contained classified information.

Bolton did eventually leave the Trump Administration (he was fired), and, like the nasty swamp creature he is, he did publish a tell-all book. The book ALSO contained classified information and was flagged by the federal government; a civil case was filed, and eventually he had to make changes.

Soon after, Iran hacked his email and acquired all of the classified information he had transmitted through Gmail.

Years later, the U.S. became aware of Iran possessing the classified material. Investigators realized it was from Bolton's email, which led to an investigation that resulted in the 18 charges brought in October 2025.

Now, some 8 months later, Bolton is changing his plea.
